questions.stem: A notebook fails with an error that a column can't be resolved. The column exists in the source file. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: V-Order is turned off
The name in the code doesn't match the DataFrame's schema, for example different spelling or a column lost in an earlier select
The Spark pool is too small
The lakehouse is in a different domain

questions.explanation: An unresolved column error means the plan refers to a column the DataFrame doesn't have at that point. Print the schema before the failing step.

questions.stem: A notebook fails with an out-of-memory error on the driver at df.toPandas() on a large table. What is the best fix?

options.text: Turn off autoscale
Aggregate or filter in Spark first, and bring only the small result to the driver
Use collect() instead
Call toPandas() twice

questions.explanation: toPandas and collect pull all the data onto the driver. Keep the work distributed in Spark and only bring small results back.

questions.stem: A notebook fails with ModuleNotFoundError for a package it imports. The package must be available to every run, including scheduled ones. What should you do?

options.text: Rename the import
Install it on your PC
Add the package to an environment and attach the environment to the notebook or workspace
Run the notebook again

questions.explanation: An environment's libraries are installed in every session that uses it, including scheduled runs. An in-session install lasts only for that session.

questions.stem: A notebook works when you run it, but fails with a path-not-found error on Files/raw/orders.csv when it's run from another workspace with no default lakehouse attached. Which path works wherever it runs?

options.text: `https://<workspace>.blob.core.windows.net/orders.csv`
`C:/Files/raw/orders.csv`
`/lakehouse/orders.csv` on the driver's local disk
`abfss://<workspace>@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/<lakehouse>.Lakehouse/Files/raw/orders.csv`

questions.explanation: A relative Files/ path depends on the lakehouse attached to the notebook. A full OneLake address names the workspace and item, so it resolves the same way from any notebook with access to the data.

questions.stem: A notebook's session fails to start with `Spark_User_Conda_PipFailed`. The environment pins a library version that conflicts with a package already installed in the Fabric runtime. What should you try?

options.text: Turn on V-Order for the session
Run the notebook in high concurrency mode
Increase spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
Remove the version pin so pip can resolve a compatible version

questions.explanation: PipFailed can come from a version conflict with pre-installed packages; removing the pin lets pip resolve a compatible version. Session mode, V-Order and shuffle partitions don't affect library installation.

questions.stem: A notebook that calls a Scala library fails with `Spark_User_UserApp_ClassNotFound`. The library's JAR isn't installed. What fixes it?

options.text: Restart the session with a smaller node size
Run OPTIMIZE on the source table
Convert the notebook cell to Spark SQL
Upload the JAR to the Fabric environment or attach it to the session

questions.explanation: ClassNotFound means a class isn't on the classpath, typically a missing library; you add the JAR to the environment or attach it with %%configure. The other options don't add the class.

questions.stem: A notebook fails with `Spark_Ambiguous_UserApp_JobAborted`. Where do you find the real reason the stage failed?

options.text: In the Capacity Metrics app's Storage page
In the workspace's sensitivity label settings
In the Spark UI, on the Stages tab, by selecting the failed stage and reviewing the task failure reason
In the lakehouse's table properties

questions.explanation: JobAborted wraps the real error; you review the failed stage's task failure reason in the Spark UI Stages tab. The other places don't show task failures.

questions.stem: A scheduled notebook fails with `Spark_Ambiguous_MsSparkUtils_EmptyString` at this line: `notebookutils.fs.ls(folder)`. The `folder` parameter is set by the pipeline, but this run passed no value. What is the best fix?

options.text: Give the folder parameter a default value and check it isn't empty before the call
Replace notebookutils.fs.ls with df.toPandas()
Run the notebook in a different workspace
Increase the driver memory

questions.explanation: The error means a notebookutils function got an empty string; you make sure parameters are non-empty and provide default values. Memory or workspace changes don't fix an empty argument.

questions.stem: A data scientist's cell uses `randomSplit()` on a DataFrame, and the Spark advisor shows a warning in the cell output. What does the advisor recommend?

options.text: Run OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY on the source table
Cache the DataFrame before using randomSplit()
Replace randomSplit() with a broadcast join
Disable the Spark advisor for the workspace

questions.explanation: The Spark advisor warns that randomSplit can return inconsistent results and recommends caching before calling it. The other options don't address the inconsistency.

questions.stem: A notebook job fails with executor crashes. Which two checks in the Spark UI match the Fabric troubleshooting guidance? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Check exit codes in the Executors tab
Detect data skew in the lakehouse explorer
Review memory usage in the Jobs tab's DAG view only
Check exit codes in the Environment tab
Detect data skew in the Stages tab

questions.explanation: The guide names checking exit codes in the Executors tab and detecting data skew in the Stages tab (and memory usage in the Storage tab). The other tabs and tools aren't where it points.
